source_audit.finding: Tamsin Vera Kestell’s 2 March enquiry names Ivor Ellis Kestell and reports his death, address, the papers she held, her executor nomination, the outright residuary gift and the pending balance request. It does not state that she is his daughter and does not independently prove a graph edge.

The 5 March update identifies Leonie Tess Rindle and Nella Ruth Verrow as distinct contacts and records the reported name checks, living status and relay arrangements. It neither identifies the speaker in DP-7316 nor states a scored family relationship.

The native relay provides the father statement, Kellan Hugh Sorrel’s full name and the conversation reference, date and time. The shared destination is not a speaker identifier. This Source supports the edge only when joined to m5x7.

Merrin Vale’s extract, issued 13 March, supplies the identity link through the completed sole-attendee row for DP-7316. It distinguishes Leonie Tess Rindle from nominated packet recipient Tamsin Vera Kestell. It contains no conversation text and cannot prove parentage alone.

Tamsin’s inline forward supplies the same referenced father statement and can substitute for r8c3 in the join to m5x7. Tamsin expressly disclaims attendance and personal reporting. The forward is not independent corroboration.

Orla Fenwick’s sighting record gives two distinct routes to the Ivor-to-Tamsin parent edge: the certified birth entry and Ivor’s daughter wording in the signed original will. It also reports the death entry, outright residue and return of all three papers.

Seth Calder’s 26 March intake note is independently sufficient as a Source for the Ivor-to-Tamsin edge, through either underlying record and the locally resolved short names. It does not add new underlying parentage records. It confirms the relay copies’ common origin and availability, the intake sighting and return, the contact instructions, the absence of an application started at intake and the outstanding balance confirmation. It does not identify the DP-7316 attendee or state the father claim on its own.
